unlisted_practices: AI-supported double reading versus standard double reading in population mammography screening, with radiologists voluntarily choosing whether to use AI

links.outcome: Radiologists' breast cancer detection with versus without AI support
links.effect: Detection was 6.7 versus 5.7 per 1,000, 17.6% higher with AI (95% confidence interval: +5.7%, +30.8%). AI use was voluntary, not randomized.
links.quote: Radiologists in the AI-supported screening group achieved a breast cancer detection rate of 6.7 per 1,000, which was 17.6% (95% confidence interval: +5.7%, +30.8%) higher than and statistically superior to the rate (5.7 per 1,000) achieved in the control group.

links.outcome: Cancer detection and recall rates versus standard double reading
links.effect: Cancer detection increased 17.6%. Recall was 37.4 versus 38.3 per 1,000, meeting noninferiority (percentage difference: -2.5% (-6.5%, +1.7%)).
links.quote: The recall rate in the AI group was 37.4 per 1,000, which was lower than and noninferior to that (38.3 per 1,000) in the control group (percentage difference: -2.5% (-6.5%, +1.7%)).
